points.why: It warns the score may be uncalibrated or drifted, but it still treats the score as a valid basis for routing once calibrated, instead of saying self-reported confidence shouldn't set scrutiny.
It says the low problem count may just reflect that nobody looks at auto-approved claims, so the clean record isn't evidence of accuracy.
It recommends a permanent random audit across all score bands with blind adjusters, but never says to set scrutiny by stakes or decision type.
It never proposes deterministic rule gates such as amount limits or coverage checks.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly says the clean record doesn't support lowering the threshold yet.
